title: Veterinarian Salary Guide: Award Rates, Hourly Pay, and Annual Earnings
description: Understand veterinarian salary under the Animal Care Award. See hourly rates for Level 1A to Level 4, annual conversion, casual loading, super, and tax.
salarySummary: A veterinary surgeon Level 1A earns $34.20 per hour, or $1,299.60 per week based on 38 hours, equating to approximately $67,582 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual veterinarian salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours (typically 38 for full-time under the award) and then by 52 weeks. For example, a Level 1A veterinary surgeon on $34.20 per hour working 38 hours per week earns $34.20 × 38 = $1,299.60 per week, and $1,299.60 × 52 = $67,579.20 per year. Use [the timesheet](/) to try different rates.

faqs.q: What is casual loading for veterinarians and how does it affect pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the minimum hourly rate, paid instead of leave entitlements. For a Level 1A veterinary surgeon, the casual rate is $34.20 × 1.25 = $42.75 per hour. This loading is added on top of the base rate – do not enter a rate that already includes it. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid separately?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your hourly rate. Under the award and the Super Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings to a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27). For a Level 1A veterinarian earning $67,582, that adds about $8,110 in super per year. Learn more at [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Veterinarian Salary Under the Animal Care Award

If you are a veterinary surgeon in Australia, your minimum pay is set by the **Animal Care and Veterinary Services Award 2020** [MA000118]. This award covers practice managers, veterinary nurses, receptionists, and veterinary surgeons. For veterinarians, the classification structure runs from Level 1A to Level 4, each with a minimum hourly rate. This guide explains how to convert those hourly rates into a weekly, fortnightly, and annual veterinarian salary, and what to expect for tax and super.

### Award Rates for Veterinary Surgeons

According to the Fair Work Ombudsman, the minimum hourly rates for full-time and part-time veterinary surgeons from 1 July 2026 are:

| Classification | Annual Salary | Hourly Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1A | $67,582 | $34.20 |
| Level 1B | $71,300 | $36.08 |
| Level 2 | $77,032 | $38.98 |
| Level 3 | $84,628 | $42.83 |
| Level 4 | $95,593 | $48.38 |

These rates are for ordinary hours – an average of 38 per week. The annual salary is calculated by dividing by 52 and then by 38 to get the hourly figure. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, so a casual Level 1A earns $42.75 per hour. provides the full award.

### Converting Hourly Rate to Annual Veterinarian Salary

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

Assuming a 38-hour week (the award standard for full-time), a Level 1A veterinarian earning $34.20 per hour would have:

- Weekly pay: $34.20 × 38 = $1,299.60
- Fortnightly pay: $1,299.60 × 2 = $2,599.20
- Annual gross: $1,299.60 × 52 = $67,579.20 (rounds to the award annual salary of $67,582)

This calculation works for any hourly rate. If you are part-time, use your agreed weekly hours instead of 38. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page has more examples.

### Casual Loading and How It Works

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave (annual, personal, etc.). The loading is applied to the base rate – you should never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator. For a Level 2 veterinarian, the base rate is $38.98, so the casual rate is $38.98 × 1.25 = $48.73 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide explains the rules.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings to a super fund (for 2026–27). This is paid on top of your hourly rate, not deducted from it. For a Level 1A veterinarian earning $67,582, the super contribution would be about $8,110 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The award also specifies that contributions must go to a fund like AustralianSuper unless the employee chooses another. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a Level 1A veterinarian earning $67,582, the tax would be approximately $11,067 plus Medicare $1,352, leaving about $55,163 after tax (excluding HELP or surcharges). Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page to estimate your net income.

### Comparing with National Minimum Wage and Average Earnings

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates for veterinarians start well above this. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026). A Level 4 veterinarian at $48.38 per hour earns $1,838.44 per week, which is below that average but reflects the award minimum – many veterinarians earn more through experience or enterprise agreements.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more accurate calculations, use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. The [pay guides](/blog) page links to official Fair Work summaries.
